bug.description: Chained at-to-at walk edges let the planner string together many stop-to-stop hops (each under TRANSFER_RADIUS_M=100) into one long walk, so a "transfer" step reports walk_m far above the transfer radius (511 m Pampang to Angeles Sapangbato Terminal via 7 hops). The same chaining happens in the pre-ride and post-ride walk sections. Each edge meets criterion 1, but the whole walk contradicts the intent that transfers walk at most TRANSFER_RADIUS_M, and it is far beyond WALK_RADIUS_M-style limits.
bug.reproduction: Run the service on the seeded DB: curl "http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/plan?from_lat=15.1621338&from_lng=120.6079997&to_lat=15.1482&to_lng=120.5744" -> steps contain {"type":"transfer","from":"Pampang","to":"Angeles Sapangbato Terminal","walk_m":511,"to_color":"red"}. Path walks pampang-puregold-young_bookstore-jollibee_rizal_street-dainty_china_house-diamond_home_plaza-addessa-angeles_sapangbato_terminal.

bug.description: When start and end are near the same stop (no ride), the response is two walk steps "Walk to Pampang, walk to your destination." This follows the recorded assumption, so it is not a spec violation, but it is awkward UX; reported for the user's decision only.

verification.self_critique: Did not run the GitHub CI or Docker image build. no_route and empty-data behavior were verified only through the existing tests, not live. Concurrency (criterion 2 under threads) not stress-tested. The chained-walk finding depends on the real seed's dense stop spacing. Seeding changed the dev database "biyahe" (re-runnable, expected).
